subject: API edge instability — incident advisory and post-incident checklist
messages:
From: Tessa Morgan <tessa_morgan@redwood.ai>
To: ops@brightleaf.com, statusteam@brightleaf.com
Cc: Sean Gallagher <sean_gallagher@redwood.ai>, Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.ai>
Date: Fri, 13 Nov 2026 09:12:00 -0800
Subject: [Status] Investigating degraded API responses in US-WEST (initial advisory)

Hi BrightLeaf ops team —

We are investigating a spike in errors and elevated p95 latency for hosted inference requests originating from our US-West (us-west1) edge cluster. Symptoms observed: short connection resets, partial streaming responses, and tokenization stalls for long-streaming sessions. Impact window began ~08:45 PT and currently affects ~7% of requests routed to us-west.

What we have done so far:
- Automatically routed new traffic away from the affected us-west edge pool to us-east while we triage.
- Enabled additional retry/backoff logic for long streaming sessions.
- Opened an incident on our status page: https://status.redwood.ai/incidents/INC-20261113-USW1

Please share any logs or observed client-side errors (request ids, timestamps). We will provide a timeline and an initial mitigation note in the next 60–90 minutes. Attached is a short CSV with request sampling we pulled (edge-timeline-20261113.csv).

Apologies for the disruption — we know this impacts your user flows. I will keep you updated on scope and ETA for a full resolution.

Thanks,
Tessa
Tessa Morgan
Account Lead, Customer Reliability
Redwood Inference

Attachment: edge-timeline-20261113.csv (csv)

From: Sean Gallagher <sean_gallagher@redwood.ai>
To: Tessa Morgan <tessa_morgan@redwood.ai>, Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.ai>, Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.ai>, ops@brightleaf.com
Date: Fri, 13 Nov 2026 10:05:00 -0800
Subject: Re: [Status] Investigating degraded API responses in US-WEST (initial advisory)

Tessa — quick update from the runtime/infra side.

Root symptom (current hypothesis): control-plane autoscaler triggered an unusually large rebalancing against a subset of edge proxies because of a delayed health-check signal. That induced transient TCP connection resets as proxies drained connections while the pool reconfigured.

Immediate actions taken (10:00 PT):
- Rolled back the latest autoscaler tuning change (reverted commit rfa3c2).
- Disabled aggressive proxy drain on the us-west pool to avoid mid-request resets.
- Increased headroom on the us-west warm pool while we validate health-check timing.

Customer-visible: we expect request success rate to return to baseline in the next ~25–40 minutes as in-flight rebalances complete. We have routed new traffic to us-east but left existing sessions in place with added retry logic.

Suggested external message: short update with expected recovery window and that we will publish a post-incident summary by EOD. I can prepare the technical appendix for the postmortem (timeline + kernel logs).

Thanks for the updates — appreciate the quick response. A few asks from BrightLeaf ops:

1) Can you confirm whether any request payloads were truncated or lost permanently (we saw a handful of partial responses that caused ingestion retries on our end)?
2) When will you have an RCA and a customer-facing postmortem? Our support team needs to advise impacted customers on SLA/credits expectations.
3) If you are routing traffic to us-east, are there latency regressions for our users in the west (we saw a small uptick in 95th percentile after the reroute)?

If helpful, we can share representative request-ids — I attached a short sample in my reply. Please provide an estimated timeline for the postmortem publication; our PMs expect a brief summary within the next business day.

— James Park
Sr. Platform Ops, BrightLeaf Analytics

From: Tessa Morgan <tessa_morgan@redwood.ai>
To: James Park <j.park@brightleaf.com>, ops@brightleaf.com
Cc: Sean Gallagher <sean_gallagher@redwood.ai>, Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.ai>, Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.ai>
Date: Fri, 13 Nov 2026 15:45:00 -0800
Subject: [Resolved] US-WEST edge instability — resolution, timeline & next steps

Hi James and BrightLeaf team —

Status: Resolved (15:30 PT). The control-plane autoscaler rollback and disabling of aggressive proxy drain stopped the mid-request resets; we observed success rate return to baseline by ~15:10 PT after in-flight drains completed. We have closed the immediate mitigation and are running validation traffic to the us-west pool.

Summary and immediate customer-facing notes:
- Impact window: 2026-11-13 08:45 PT — 2026-11-13 15:10 PT (US-WEST requests experienced elevated p95 and intermittent partial streaming responses).
- Root cause (short): autoscaler reconfiguration produced premature drain signals on a subset of edge proxies, causing connection resets for in-flight streaming sessions.
- Customer impact: approximately 7% of hosted inference requests routed to us-west experienced errors or partial responses. No data deletion or exfiltration observed.

Attached: postmortem-draft-v1.md (internal draft) and edge-timeline-20261113.csv. Public postmortem & status page update will be published by EOD PST; I will share the public link here when available.

Next steps (action items):
- Marcus: finalize kernel/log appendix and add sample request-ids (ETA: EOD).
- Laura: draft customer-facing postmortem language and coordinate publishing on the status page (ETA: 3 hours).
- Sean: follow-up change to autoscaler default and add a safe-guard to prevent aggressive proxy drains in production (ETA: next sprint).

We will also offer BrightLeaf a credit for the partial degradation window; Laura will coordinate with your billing team on details.

Thanks again for the patience and the sample logs — they helped narrow the scope quickly.

Tessa Morgan
Account Lead, Customer Reliability
Redwood Inference

Attachments: postmortem-draft-v1.md (markdown), edge-timeline-20261113.csv (csv)
